generic: ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 Corona Virus Vaccine (Recombinant) - Covishield / AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine
cls: Vaccine (recombinant replication-deficient chimpanzee adenovirus-vectored COVID-19 vaccine)
pharm: Replication-deficient chimpanzee adenovirus (ChAdOx1) vector encoding the full-length SARS-CoV-2 spike (S) glycoprotein; induces spike-specific humoral and cellular immunity against SARS-CoV-2.
quick: 0.5 mL intramuscular per dose; two-dose primary series
Use when potential benefits outweigh risks; per local public-health guidance
May be given to breastfeeding women per public-health guidance
Observe 15-30 min post-injection for hypersensitivity; watch for TTS symptoms
summary: ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 (marketed as Covishield in India and as the AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine/Vaxzevria) is a recombinant, replication-deficient chimpanzee adenovirus-vectored vaccine encoding the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. It is given as a 0.5 mL intramuscular injection in a two-dose primary series to prevent COVID-19. Common reactions are injection-site pain, fatigue, headache, myalgia, and fever. A rare but serious risk is thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome (TTS); rare cases of capillary leak syndrome and Guillain-Barre syndrome have also been reported. This vaccine received WHO Emergency Use Listing and national authorizations; it is not US FDA-approved (see pearls).
indications: Active immunization to prevent coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) caused by SARS-CoV-2 in individuals 18 years of age and older

dosage.d: 0.5 mL (one dose) intramuscularly, preferably in the deltoid
0.5 mL given 4-12 weeks (28-84 days) after the first dose
dosage.n: Longer interval (8-12 weeks) associated with higher efficacy

dosage.d: 0.5 mL as recommended by national immunization guidance

admin: Administer by intramuscular injection only, preferably into the deltoid muscle
Do not administer intravenously, intradermally, or subcutaneously
Multidose vial: withdraw each 0.5 mL dose using aseptic technique; do not pool excess vaccine
Have appropriate medical treatment available to manage anaphylaxis; observe recipients after vaccination
Do not freeze; store refrigerated and use within the labeled period once the vial is opened
moa: The vaccine consists of a replication-deficient chimpanzee adenovirus (ChAdOx1) vector carrying the genetic code for the full-length SARS-CoV-2 spike (S) glycoprotein. After intramuscular injection, the vector enters host cells and the spike gene is transcribed and translated, leading to local expression of the spike protein. This stimulates both neutralizing antibody responses against the spike protein and spike-specific T-cell responses, providing immunity that helps prevent SARS-CoV-2 infection and COVID-19 disease. The adenoviral vector is replication-deficient and cannot cause infection or integrate into the genome.

absolute: Known severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) to a previous dose or to any vaccine component
History of thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome (TTS) following a previous dose of this or another adenovirus-vectored COVID-19 vaccine
relative: History of thrombosis combined with thrombocytopenia (e.g., heparin-induced thrombocytopenia) - benefit-risk assessment
Bleeding disorders or anticoagulant therapy (intramuscular injection precautions)
Acute severe febrile illness (defer until recovery)
monitor: Immediate hypersensitivity in the 15-30 minutes after injection
Symptoms of thrombosis with thrombocytopenia (severe/persistent headache, blurred vision, dyspnea, chest/abdominal pain, leg swelling, petechiae) in the weeks after vaccination
Signs of capillary leak syndrome and Guillain-Barre syndrome

preg: There are limited data on use in pregnancy. Administration during pregnancy should be considered when the potential benefits outweigh any potential risks, in line with national public-health recommendations. Animal reproductive studies did not show harmful effects.
lact: It is not known whether the vaccine is excreted in human milk; given that it is non-replicating, it is considered unlikely to pose a risk to the breastfed infant. The vaccine may be given to breastfeeding women per public-health guidance.
renal: No dose adjustment is required in renal impairment.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required in hepatic impairment.

moderate: Immunosuppressive therapy (high-dose corticosteroids, chemotherapy, biologics) may reduce the immune response to the vaccine
minor: Co-administration with other vaccines should follow national immunization guidance
interactions.diagnostics: Can cause transient lymphopenia and, rarely, thrombocytopenia; consider in the interpretation of post-vaccination blood counts.

emergency: Thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome (TTS) with cerebral or splanchnic thrombosis
Acute Guillain-Barre syndrome with respiratory compromise

monitoring: Observe recipients for 15-30 minutes after vaccination for immediate hypersensitivity

Educate recipients to seek care for symptoms of thrombosis with thrombocytopenia within ~3 weeks (severe headache, visual changes, shortness of breath, chest/abdominal/leg pain, easy bruising/petechiae)
Monitor for neurological symptoms suggestive of Guillain-Barre syndrome
counsel: This is a two-dose vaccine to help prevent COVID-19; complete the series as advised
Mild side effects such as a sore arm, tiredness, headache, muscle aches, and fever are common and usually settle within a few days

Seek urgent medical attention if, within about 3 weeks of vaccination, you have a severe or persistent headache, blurred vision, shortness of breath, chest or stomach pain, leg swelling, or unusual bruising/tiny red spots
Tell the vaccinator about any severe allergies or a previous reaction to a vaccine
Vaccination does not give immediate or complete protection; continue recommended precautions
pk: Immune response develops over ~2-3 weeks after the first dose; protection increases after the second dose
Antibody and T-cell responses peak in the weeks following the second dose
Not applicable (vaccine; induces durable adaptive immunity)
Protective immunity wanes over months; boosters per public-health guidance
Store at 2-8 C; do not freeze; protect from light; do not use beyond labeled in-use period after first puncture
pearls: This vaccine is not US FDA-approved; it received WHO Emergency Use Listing and national authorizations (Covishield in India; Vaxzevria/AstraZeneca elsewhere) - guidance based on WHO and manufacturer/regulator information
Rare thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome (TTS) typically presents 4-28 days after vaccination - educate recipients on warning symptoms
Longer dosing interval (8-12 weeks) between the two doses is associated with higher vaccine efficacy
Contraindicated in those with prior TTS or capillary leak syndrome after an adenovirus-vectored COVID-19 vaccine
It is a replication-deficient adenovirus vector and cannot cause COVID-19 infection
missed: If the second dose is delayed, give it as soon as possible; there is no need to restart the series. Follow national immunization guidance for the recommended interval (4-12 weeks) and any booster schedule.
overdose: Overdose (administration of more than the recommended volume) has limited data; manage with supportive care and monitoring. Increased reactogenicity (local and systemic reactions) may occur with a higher-than-recommended dose.
